Pure Autonomic Failure

Complex MONDO:0018608 Pathograph 63 Show in embeddings browser Synucleinopathy Autonomic Nervous System Disorder Neurodegenerative Disease

Pure autonomic failure (PAF; Bradbury-Eggleston syndrome, idiopathic orthostatic hypotension) is a rare, sporadic, slowly progressive adult-onset alpha-synucleinopathy in which misfolded alpha-synuclein accumulates predominantly in peripheral autonomic neurons. Degeneration and dysfunction of postganglionic sympathetic noradrenergic neurons cause a profound deficit in norepinephrine synthesis and release, so that baroreflex-mediated vasoconstriction fails on standing. The clinical picture is dominated by disabling neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, often with paradoxical supine hypertension, accompanied by bladder, bowel, sexual and sudomotor failure, but without motor or cognitive signs of central neurodegeneration. PAF is frequently a prodromal state: about a third of patients phenoconvert to Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, or multiple system atrophy over several years of follow-up. Treatment is symptomatic and aimed at orthostatic symptoms; no disease-modifying therapy exists.

Mechanistic Hypotheses

Lewy-Body PAF with Postganglionic Noradrenergic Lesion
lewy_body_paf CANONICAL
Evidence balance 1 support
Most PAF is a peripheral Lewy body disease: intraneuronal alpha-synuclein aggregates in postganglionic sympathetic neurons cause noradrenergic denervation and very low norepinephrine. This form can phenoconvert to Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, but not to MSA.

Non-Lewy PAF as Premotor Multiple System Atrophy
prodromal_msa_paf ALTERNATIVE
Evidence balance 4 support
A minority of patients diagnosed with PAF have a preganglionic lesion without the postganglionic noradrenergic lesion: higher supine norepinephrine, normal cardiac sympathetic imaging, preserved smell, younger onset, severe bladder failure, raised CSF neurofilament light chain and an MSA-like seeding profile. These patients are in the premotor phase of MSA rather than having a peripheral Lewy body disease.

Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity as the Trigger for Aggregation
catecholaldehyde_autotoxicity EMERGING
Evidence balance 2 support 1 no evidence
Aggregation in PAF is not the first event. On this account the initiating step is a shift of dopamine from vesicular stores into the cytoplasm, where monoamine oxidase produces the autotoxic aldehyde DOPAL; DOPAL then oligomerizes alpha-synuclein, and the oligomers further degrade vesicular storage, forming a positive feedback loop that destroys the neuron over a long preclinical period. The hypothesis is attractive for PAF because it explains the cell-type selectivity of the lesion, and because the vesicular storage defect it requires is independently measured in PAF patients. What is missing is any measurement of DOPAL in PAF neurons, and testing in animals has been obstructed by the secondary effects of the drugs used to manipulate the pathway. It is recorded as EMERGING for that reason, and the edges belonging to it are tagged so they can be read separately from the canonical chain.
Pathograph links
Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons -> Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation INDIRECT UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATES DOPAL oligomerizes and quinonizes alpha-synuclein, which is proposed as the proximate chemical cause of aggregation in catecholaminergic neurons. The steps between an oligomer formed in vitro and a Lewy body in a human sympathetic ganglion are not established.
Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect -> Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons INDIRECT UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATES Failing vesicular sequestration returns dopamine to the cytoplasm, where monoamine oxidase converts it to DOPAL, so the storage defect feeds the autotoxic step that is proposed to have caused it. This closes a self-reinforcing loop rather than adding a one-way step, and the loop is the form in which the catecholaldehyde hypothesis is stated. The vesicular defect is measured in PAF patients; its consequence for DOPAL levels in those patients is not.

Sympathetic-Predominant Body-First Origin of the Pathology
sympathetic_body_first_origin EMERGING
Evidence balance 2 support
Where the pathology starts, as distinct from what makes it start. Postmortem staging of Lewy body disease separates cases whose pathology appears first in peripheral autonomic tissue (body-first) from those where it appears first in the olfactory bulb and amygdala (brain-first), and splits the body-first group again into a vagal-predominant and a sympathetic-predominant subtype in roughly equal numbers. A purely peripheral, sympathetically dominated synucleinopathy, which is what PAF is, fits the sympathetic-predominant subtype, and this would make PAF the clinically isolated form of a distribution pattern that is otherwise observed on its way to Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. The evidence is autopsy-based and drawn from cohorts classified as incidental Lewy body disease, PD or DLB; no PAF case series has been staged this way, so the alignment is inferred rather than shown.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:40082617 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"we identified two distinct body-first subtypes, one with vagal predominance and another with sympathetic predominance, in equal proportions"
Establishes a sympathetic-predominant peripheral-onset subtype in 302 autopsied Lewy-positive cases. None was a PAF case, which is why this is indirect.
PMID:40082617 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"In body-first LBD, isolated Lewy pathology in the sympathetic PNS is frequent, suggesting that the gut-to-sympathetic propagation route is as important as the vagal gut-to-DMV propagation route."
Isolated sympathetic pathology with no central involvement is the anatomical counterpart of the PAF phenotype, and it is common rather than exceptional.

What starts alpha-synuclein aggregating in peripheral autonomic neurons in PAF, and does the catecholaldehyde DOPAL accumulate in those neurons before the aggregates appear?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN paf_what_initiates_aggregation
Attached to
pathophysiology#Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons pathophysiology#Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation mechanistic_hypotheses#catecholaldehyde_autotoxicity
The entry's canonical chain begins at aggregation, and the aggregation node says the initiating trigger is unknown. The catecholaldehyde node upstream of it rests on cell-free chemistry, postmortem tissue from other Lewy body diseases and a computational model; nothing has measured DOPAL, aldehyde dehydrogenase activity or the DOPAC:DOPAL ratio in sympathetic tissue from patients with PAF. The gap matters for more than completeness, because the two interventions the hypothesis implies - inhibiting monoamine oxidase to make less DOPAL, and antioxidant treatment to stop its oxidation - are both available, and PAF is the one Lewy body disease where the affected neurons are accessible by skin and vein biopsy. The author of the hypothesis lists the PAF form of the question explicitly as unanswered.
Proposed experiments
Catecholaldehyde measurement in biopsied sympathetic tissue from PAF patients
paf_dopal_in_accessible_sympathetic_tissue
Quantify DOPAL, DOPAC, the DOPAC:DOPAL ratio and aldehyde dehydrogenase activity in forearm vein and skin biopsies from patients with PAF, from patients with the non-Lewy preganglionic form, and from controls, in the same samples used to assay tyrosine hydroxylase and VMAT2. The vein-biopsy protocol that established the vesicular storage defect in PAF already yields the tissue; what has not been measured is the aldehyde.

Reconstruction of the catecholaldehyde loop in human iPSC-derived sympathetic neurons
paf_dopal_loop_in_ipsc_sympathetic_neurons
Impose the aldehyde burden on the cell type this entry is about. Human pluripotent stem cells are differentiated to postganglionic sympathetic neurons, aldehyde dehydrogenase is inhibited to raise DOPAL without adding it from outside, and alpha-synuclein oligomer load, vesicular norepinephrine storage and stimulated norepinephrine release are measured in the same cultures. The existing cell models of the catecholaldehyde step use a neuroblastoma line, mouse cortical neurons or a glial line, and supply DOPAL in the medium, so neither the affected cell type nor the endogenous route to the aldehyde has been tested; these neurons secrete norepinephrine on activation, which is the quantity PAF loses. A patient-derived line is deliberately not the design here. PAF is sporadic with no causal gene, so an unselected patient line carries no lesion to express, which is why the protocol's established use is a Mendelian autonomic disease rather than this one.
Model systems
Human iPSC-derived postganglionic sympathetic neurons
Sympathetic neurons differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells by way of neural crest, maintained as monocultures or co-cultured with iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. They carry tyrosine hydroxylase, fire action potentials, secrete norepinephrine on stimulation, and in co-culture drive the beating rate of the myocytes they innervate, so the noradrenergic functions this entry's nodes describe are all directly measurable.

Divergences from the human mechanism
cause unrepresented qualifying
PAF has no causal lesion to encode, so the aldehyde burden has to be imposed pharmacologically by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. The model therefore tests whether the loop can run, and cannot establish that it starts this way in the disease.
temporal scope qualifying
A culture runs for weeks against a disease that takes decades and whose own progression node is measured in years of serial imaging, so an acute aldehyde challenge stands in for chronic accumulation.
boundary omission immaterial
Preganglionic input, the baroreflex arc and the vasculature are outside the model. Immaterial to this experiment, whose claims are confined to events inside the postganglionic neuron.

The three readouts are read in order. An aldehyde rise followed by oligomer accumulation followed by loss of vesicular storage establishes that the loop can run in a human sympathetic neuron. Can alpha-synuclein aggregates taken from human peripheral sympathetic ganglia actually seed and propagate pathology, as the mouse fibril-injection model of PAF assumes?
HUMAN MODEL MISMATCH OPEN paf_peripheral_aggregate_seeding_mismatch
Attached to
pathophysiology#Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation pathophysiology#Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion) animal_models#Mouse
The animal model in this entry seeds pathology by injecting synthetic preformed fibrils into the ganglia of mice overexpressing mutant human alpha-synuclein, and the pathology then spreads along autonomic pathways into the central nervous system. That result is the main experimental support for the phenoconversion node. But when Lewy-body aggregates purified from the stellate ganglia of Parkinson disease patients were inoculated into mouse brain, they produced neither pathology nor degeneration, while aggregates from the same patients' substantia nigra did. So the seeding competence demonstrated in the model may be a property of synthetic fibrils in a transgenic host rather than of the human peripheral aggregate the model stands for. This is a mismatch rather than a missing experiment: evidence exists on both sides and points in opposite directions, and what is unresolved is whether the human peripheral aggregate propagates at all.

Purify alpha-synuclein aggregates from sympathetic ganglia of autopsy-confirmed PAF cases, rather than from Parkinson disease cases or from synthetic fibrils, and test them both in seed amplification assays and by inoculation into the ganglia of wild-type and TgM83 mice. The published negative result used Parkinson disease stellate ganglia and inoculated the brain, so it leaves the PAF aggregate and the peripheral route untested.

Has any environmental, occupational or lifestyle exposure been studied as a risk factor for pure autonomic failure?
KNOWLEDGE GAP no_exposure_epidemiology
Attached to
environmental#
This entry carries no environmental section because no exposure study of this disease was found, not because exposures were judged irrelevant. A deep-research sweep of exposure epidemiology across the alpha-synucleinopathies returned substantial literature for Parkinson disease, a single unreplicated case-control study for multiple system atrophy, one multicentre case-control study for isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder and one for dementia with Lewy bodies, and nothing at all for this disease. The gap matters because the exposure findings that do exist do not agree with one another across these diseases: smoking is inversely associated with Parkinson disease, positively associated with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder and null in dementia with Lewy bodies, and occupational pesticide exposure is positive in Parkinson disease and null in multiple system atrophy under a formal job-exposure matrix. Nothing can therefore be inferred about this disease from its neighbours, and an exposure profile for a condition whose pathology is largely restricted to the peripheral autonomic nervous system would bear directly on whether peripheral-onset disease has a distinct trigger.
Recorded as an absence of evidence rather than as evidence of absence. The searches run were disease-named exposure queries across the synucleinopathies; a dedicated search strategy for this disease, including its synonyms and the older Bradbury-Eggleston designation, has not been run and might surface case series that a cross-disease sweep missed.

Pathophysiology

19
Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons
Mechanism confidence: Hypothetical
Dopamine that leaks from storage vesicles into the neuronal cytoplasm is deaminated by monoamine oxidase to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (DOPAL), an obligate intermediate of dopamine metabolism normally detoxified by aldehyde dehydrogenase. DOPAL binds covalently to the lysine-rich alpha-synuclein molecule and oligomerizes it far more efficiently than dopamine itself does, and the resulting oligomers impair vesicular storage, returning more dopamine to the cytoplasm. This is the catecholaldehyde hypothesis, and it is the step put forward to explain why alpha-synuclein precipitates in catecholaminergic neurons rather than elsewhere. It is placed upstream of aggregation on in vitro, postmortem and computational grounds only: DOPAL has not been measured in sympathetic neurons of living patients, and whether it accumulates in PAF specifically is unresolved.

Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation
Misfolded, phosphorylated alpha-synuclein accumulates as Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites predominantly in peripheral autonomic neurons: sympathetic ganglion neurons and their distal axons in the heart, adrenal region, bladder and skin. CSF seeding assays are positive in nearly all patients, and cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein is found at every biopsy site. The initiating trigger is unknown. A rare clinically diagnosed case without any synuclein pathology shows that the clinical label is not always a synucleinopathy.

Preganglionic Lesion Without Postganglionic Lewy Pathology
In the minority of patients whose PAF is the premotor phase of MSA, the preganglionic autonomic lesion is not accompanied by postganglionic noradrenergic Lewy pathology. In MSA, insoluble alpha-synuclein is deposited in glia rather than as neuronal Lewy bodies. These patients have higher supine norepinephrine, a preganglionic pattern of sweat loss, severe bladder dysfunction and raised CSF neurofilament light chain, and they go on to MSA.

Preganglionic Intermediolateral Column Neuron Loss
Sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the thoracic intermediolateral cell column are lost alongside the ganglionic lesion, removing central drive to the sympathetic ganglia. Both pathological forms of PAF are thought to involve this preganglionic lesion.

Postganglionic Sympathetic Noradrenergic Denervation
Postganglionic sympathetic noradrenergic terminals are lost from the heart, renal cortex, blood vessels and skin. Cardiac 18F-dopamine and 11C-methylreboxetine PET show reduced noradrenergic innervation, and skin biopsy shows marked postganglionic denervation of autonomic adnexa, in contrast to the largely preserved peripheral innervation of MSA. Denervation is accompanied by length-dependent somatic and autonomic small-fibre loss.

Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect
Surviving sympathetic terminals store and synthesize norepinephrine poorly. Forearm vein biopsies show normal norepinephrine transporter but very low tyrosine hydroxylase and reduced VMAT2, with a raised plasma DHPG:NE ratio; PET shows rapid loss of 18F-dopamine from residual cardiac nerves. Sympathetic dysfunction may therefore precede frank denervation.

Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons Failing vesicular sequestration returns dopamine to the cytoplasm, where monoamine oxidase converts it to DOPAL, so the storage defect feeds the autotoxic step that is proposed to have caused it. This closes a self-reinforcing loop rather than adding a one-way step, and the loop is the form in which the catecholaldehyde hypothesis is stated. The vesicular defect is measured in PAF patients; its consequence for DOPAL levels in those patients is not. Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity as the Trigger for Aggregation

Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
Norepinephrine release from sympathetic terminals is profoundly reduced at rest and fails to rise on standing. Very low supine plasma norepinephrine is the biochemical signature of PAF, distinguishing it from MSA, in which postganglionic neurons are largely spared.

Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
On standing, the baroreflex cannot increase sympathetic vasoconstrictor outflow or heart rate, so peripheral resistance and venous return fall and blood pressure drops. The heart-rate rise is blunted relative to the fall in blood pressure, which is the physiological signature that separates neurogenic from non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.

Cerebral and Muscle Hypoperfusion on Standing
The upright fall in blood pressure lowers cerebral perfusion and perfusion of shoulder-girdle muscles, producing light-headedness, visual disturbance, syncope, fatigue and the suboccipital coat-hanger pain characteristic of autonomic failure. Symptoms are worse in the morning, in heat, after meals and with exertion, and resolve on lying flat.

Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation
Loss of cardiac sympathetic nerves reduces the chronotropic and inotropic reserve of the heart. Denervated hearts show an impaired inotropic response to tyramine, which depends on endogenous norepinephrine release, and exaggerated responses to the direct beta-agonist isoproterenol.

Adrenoceptor Denervation Supersensitivity
Chronic loss of sympathetic input, combined with loss of baroreflex buffering, makes patients unusually sensitive to small doses of pressor and beta-adrenergic agents. This shapes treatment: norepinephrine replacers work at low doses, while exaggerated pressor responses contribute to supine hypertension on therapy.

Supine Hypertension Mechanism
About half of patients have high blood pressure when lying flat despite very low plasma norepinephrine and suppressed renin. Raised angiotensin II and inappropriate mineralocorticoid receptor activation contribute; the full mechanism in PAF is not known.

Pelvic Visceral Autonomic Denervation
Sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation of the bladder, bowel and genital organs is affected, with Lewy bodies found in bladder-wall autonomic nerves. This produces bladder dysfunction, constipation and sexual dysfunction, which usually begin close to the onset of orthostatic hypotension.

Cardiovagal Parasympathetic Impairment
Parasympathetic cardiac (vagal) control is also impaired, reducing beat-to-beat heart-rate variation. Mild cardiovagal impairment at presentation is instead a predictor of conversion to MSA, so the degree of cardiovagal failure helps separate peripheral Lewy-body PAF from prodromal MSA.

Subclinical Central Catecholaminergic Involvement
Even without motor signs, Lewy pathology and catecholaminergic loss are found in the substantia nigra and locus coeruleus. Nigral dopaminergic denervation is as severe as in Parkinson disease, but striatal terminals are relatively spared, which may explain the absence of parkinsonism. Hyposmia and REM sleep behaviour disorder are the clinical markers of this central involvement.

Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion)
In a subset of patients the synucleinopathy becomes clinically manifest in the CNS, and the diagnosis changes to Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or multiple system atrophy. Lewy-body PAF with cardiac noradrenergic denervation converts to Lewy body disease, whereas PAF with preserved postganglionic innervation, higher norepinephrine and an MSA-like CSF seeding profile converts to MSA. RBD is the strongest clinical predictor of any conversion.

Salt and Fluid Loading with Rapid Water Drinking
Action: dietary salt and water loadingNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is dietary salt and water loading, annotated with Dietary Intervention (NCIT:C15447). Peripheral alpha-1 adrenoceptor agonist (prodrug of desglymidodrine) that acts directly on vascular receptors and so does not require surviving noradrenergic terminals. Taken during the day before upright activity; avoid the supine position for several hours after a dose. Adverse effects include supine hypertension, piloerection and urinary retention.

Action: PharmacotherapyNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Pharmacotherapy (NCIT:C15986). NCIT:C15986 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C15986
Agent: ampreloxetine CHEBI:757112 Chemical Entities of Biological Interest (CHEBI) Relation: this treatment uses this therapeutic agent This treatment uses ampreloxetine (CHEBI:757112). CHEBI:757112 is a therapeutic agent from Chemical Entities of Biological Interest.
Platform: Small molecule
Investigational once-daily selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that raises synaptic norepinephrine from residual sympathetic terminals. A phase 2 trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension raised seated blood pressure with little effect on supine pressure. The phase 3 SEQUOIA and REDWOOD trials, which enrolled PAF as well as PD and MSA patients, missed their primary endpoints. A prespecified MSA subgroup analysis showed maintained symptom benefit on secondary endpoints after randomized withdrawal; the trials were powered only for the full population, and no PAF-specific result has been reported. Like atomoxetine, it is expected to help least in PAF, where those neurons are lost. It is not approved.
Mechanism Target:
MODULATES Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release

Diagnosis

7
Head-up tilt or active stand blood pressure testing
Orthostatic hypotension is a sustained fall of at least 20 mmHg systolic or 10 mmHg diastolic blood pressure within 3 minutes of standing or head-up tilt. A blunted heart-rate rise (change in heart rate divided by change in systolic pressure below 0.5 bpm/mmHg) identifies a neurogenic cause. Supine blood pressure is measured at the same session to detect supine hypertension.

Progression

3
Adult-onset insidious autonomic failure
Age: Middle to late adulthood (pooled mean onset about 63 years)
Onset is insidious in adulthood or old age. Most non-orthostatic autonomic symptoms begin close to the onset of orthostatic hypotension, while dream enactment behaviour tends to appear years later.

Duration: Years to decades; median survival about 15 years from orthostatic symptom onset

Phenoconversion to a central synucleinopathy
Duration: About 5 percent per year in pooled data (12 percent per year in one prospective cohort)
Roughly a quarter to a third of patients presenting with PAF develop Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or multiple system atrophy. Conversion to MSA clusters in the first years of follow-up, whereas conversion to Lewy body disorders occurs at a steadier rate. The annual-risk estimates differ between the eight-centre prospective cohort and the meta-analysis.

Clinical Burden

High
Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension is disabling, causing recurrent syncope, falls and inability to stand for long, and is frequently complicated by supine hypertension that constrains treatment. About a third of patients go on to a central synucleinopathy. Survival is nonetheless longer than in MSA, PD or DLB.

Experimental Models

2
DOPAL challenge in BE(2)-M17 neuroblastoma cells and primary cortical neurons CELL_LINE
The non-animal system behind the catecholaldehyde step of this entry. DOPAL added to the medium forms covalent oligomers with alpha-synuclein inside the cell, and those oligomers permeabilise cholesterol-containing membranes, damage synaptic vesicles and let dopamine escape into the cytoplasm, where it is converted to more DOPAL. It is the experiment that makes the vicious cycle drawn in this entry's pathograph measurable rather than inferred, and it works on endogenous as well as overexpressed alpha-synuclein. It is not a model of PAF. The cells are a neuroblastoma line and mouse cortical neurons rather than sympathetic noradrenergic neurons, no patient material is involved, and the catecholamine that leaks is dopamine rather than norepinephrine.
Exogenous DOPAL exposure at 20 and 50 micromolar in the mouse primary neurons Exogenous DOPAL exposure at 100 micromolar in the human overexpressing lines Preformed alpha-synuclein-DOPAL oligomers at 2 micromolar for the cellular permeabilisation experiments Alpha-synuclein overexpression, and endogenous alpha-synuclein alone

Cell source
Human BE(2)-M17 neuroblastoma cells overexpressing mCherry-tagged alpha-synuclein, with mouse primary cortical neurons carrying only endogenous alpha-synuclein as the non-overexpressing comparison, both exposed to exogenous DOPAL. HEK293T cells overexpressing alpha-synuclein-EGFP are the paper's negative arm: they supply the mass-spectrometric characterisation of the modified protein, but oligomers were not detected in them. An isolated synaptic-vesicle preparation is assayed alongside the intact cells.

Two-dimensional monolayer culture, with an accompanying isolated synaptic-vesicle preparation

Pathograph links
Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons perturbs fidelity: moderate observes: molecular DOPAL is applied to intact cells and the covalent alpha-synuclein oligomers this node describes are then recovered from inside them, so the node's chemistry is demonstrated in a cellular context rather than only in a tube.
Limitations: DOPAL is supplied from outside at fixed concentrations, so the node's claim that it accumulates because dopamine leaks from storage vesicles and is deaminated in the cytoplasm is assumed by the design rather than tested by it.
Divergences from the human mechanism
cause unrepresented qualifying
The node's upstream cause is vesicular leak followed by monoamine oxidase deamination of cytoplasmic dopamine. Here the aldehyde is pipetted into the medium, so neither the leak nor the enzymatic step is in the model, and the exposure cannot be titrated to a physiological cytoplasmic concentration.
boundary omission qualifying
A sympathetic noradrenergic neuron is outside the model. Its distinguishing features - dopamine beta-hydroxylase inside the vesicle, norepinephrine rather than dopamine as the stored transmitter, and the aldehyde dehydrogenase complement of that cell type - are exactly what the node invokes to explain why catecholaminergic neurons are selectively affected.
species mismatch qualifying
The non-overexpressing arm uses mouse cortical neurons, and the species gap bears on this link because the endogenous-alpha-synuclein claim rests on that arm alone. Both human lines overexpress a tagged construct, and in the HEK293T line no oligomers were detected at all, so there is no human result showing the reaction on endogenous protein at endogenous abundance. The substrate in the neurons is the mouse protein rather than the human one, and those neurons were exposed to 20 or 50 micromolar DOPAL against 100 micromolar in the human lines, so the two arms are not interchangeable on dose either.
Readouts
Covalent alpha-synuclein oligomer formation after DOPAL exposure
Direction: INCREASED
Interpretation: Oligomeric alpha-synuclein species appear on western blot in DOPAL-treated cells and not in untreated ones, in both the overexpressing line and neurons carrying only endogenous protein.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:28084443 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"is able to induce aS oligomerization in immortalized cell lines, and in primary neurons"
The measurement behind this readout, in both cell systems.
Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect partially recapitulates fidelity: low observes: cellular Catecholamine escaping from storage vesicles is the quantity this node is about, and it is measured here as a consequence of the aldehyde-driven oligomers rather than assumed. That is the return arm of the loop this entry draws between the storage defect and the catecholaldehyde node.
Limitations: The transmitter that leaks is dopamine from a neuroblastoma line and from cortical neurons, not norepinephrine from a sympathetic neuron, and vesicular monoamine transporter density and tyrosine hydroxylase content - the two measurements that define this node in patients - are not reported.
Divergences from the human mechanism
proxy quantity qualifying
Dopamine leak from synaptic vesicles stands in for failure of norepinephrine sequestration in a sympathetic varicosity. The direction of the defect is the same; the transmitter, the vesicle population and the cell are not.
boundary omission qualifying
Dopamine beta-hydroxylase and the noradrenergic vesicle itself lie outside the model, so nothing here bears on the reduced vesicular norepinephrine synthesis that this node also asserts.
species mismatch qualifying
The in-cell evidence that oligomers damage synaptic vesicles is the electron microscopy of mouse primary neurons, where the readily releasable pool shrinks and vesicles per synapse fall from about 71 to 49 and 38 with rising DOPAL. The human arm contributes the pHluorin permeabilisation result and the dopamine-leak assay is cell-free, so the structural measurement of vesicle loss has no human counterpart here.
Readouts
Dopamine leak from synaptic vesicles
Direction: INCREASED
Interpretation: Alpha-synuclein-DOPAL oligomers permeabilise vesicle membranes and release stored dopamine, in isolated vesicles and in cells.

MO3.13 oligodendrocyte and PC12 catecholaldehyde transfer co-culture CO_CULTURE
A catecholamine-free recipient cell used as a clean background for the aldehyde. It answers a question the single-cell systems cannot: whether DOPAL made in one cell reaches another and oligomerises alpha-synuclein there. It was built to explain glial inclusions in multiple system atrophy, so for PAF it bears on the chemistry and the transmissibility and not on the cell type, and the entry's other MO3.13 result on DOPAL-driven quinonisation of intracellular proteins comes from the same laboratory.

Pathograph links
Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons perturbs fidelity: low observes: molecular Shows the aldehyde crossing from a catecholamine-synthesising cell into a recipient that makes none, and oligomerising alpha-synuclein once inside, so the oligomerising step this node asserts does not require the aldehyde to be made in the same cell.
Limitations: The recipient is a glial line chosen for the multiple system atrophy question, and neither alpha-synuclein nor the catecholamine is endogenous to it, so the model reproduces the reaction and not the cell in which this entry places it.
Divergences from the human mechanism
boundary omission qualifying
The sympathetic noradrenergic neuron is absent, and so is the intracellular origin of the aldehyde. Alpha-synuclein is added from outside rather than expressed, so the model cannot speak to the concentrations either species reaches in the affected neuron.
proxy quantity qualifying
An oligodendrocyte taking up extracellular alpha-synuclein stands in for a peripheral noradrenergic neuron aggregating its own. The cell-type selectivity that this node exists to explain is therefore not something the model can test.
species mismatch immaterial
The dopamine-producing partner in the transfer arm is a rat PC12 line. Immaterial to the claim, because the arm with DOPAL added directly to the human cells gives the same result.

🐁

Animal Models

1
Ganglionic alpha-synuclein fibril injection in TgM83 mice
Preformed alpha-synuclein fibrils injected into the stellate and celiac ganglia of TgM83 mice spread only along autonomic pathways, to the central nervous system and bidirectionally to the autonomic innervation of peripheral organs. The mice develop orthostatic hypotension, constipation, hypohidrosis and hyposmia without motor dysfunction.
Species
Mouse
Genotype
TgM83+/- (human SNCA A53T transgene, hemizygous)
Publication
PMID:32071315
Pathograph links
Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation partially recapitulates fidelity: moderate observes: organism Autonomic-restricted alpha-synuclein pathology with autonomic failure and no motor signs, the defining features of PAF.
Limitations: Pathology is seeded by injected fibrils into mice overexpressing mutant human alpha-synuclein, whereas human PAF is sporadic with no SNCA variant, and the seeded pathology also reaches the central nervous system.
Divergences from the human mechanism
cause unrepresented qualifying
Aggregation is started by injecting preformed fibrils into ganglia of mice overexpressing A53T human alpha-synuclein. In the sporadic human disease the protein is wild type at normal dosage and the initiating trigger is unknown, so the model cannot speak to why aggregation begins.
species mismatch qualifying
Orthostatic hypotension and hypohidrosis are measured in mice, whose postural cardiovascular load differs greatly from upright humans.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:32071315 SUPPORT Model Organism
"In parallel, the mice develop autonomic dysfunction, featured by orthostatic hypotension, constipation, hypohidrosis and hyposmia, without motor dysfunction."
The model reproduces autonomic failure without motor features.
Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion) partially recapitulates fidelity: low observes: organism Pathology spreads from autonomic ganglia to the central nervous system.
Limitations: Central spread was shown histologically without the motor or cognitive phenotype of a phenoconverted disease, and the model has not been shown to separate Lewy-type from MSA-type conversion.
Divergences from the human mechanism
proxy quantity qualifying
The model's quantity is the histological presence of alpha-synuclein pathology in central regions. The node's quantity is clinical phenoconversion to Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, which is a diagnosis made on motor or cognitive features the mice never develop. Central pathology stands in for a clinical event, and the proportion of PAF patients with central pathology who would ever convert is not something this model can report.
cause unrepresented qualifying
Spread is initiated by synthetic preformed fibrils in a host overexpressing A53T human alpha-synuclein. Aggregates purified from human sympathetic ganglia have failed to seed pathology in mouse brain, so whether the human peripheral aggregate propagates as this model's fibrils do is unsettled; see the paf_peripheral_aggregate_seeding_mismatch discussion.

PMID:32071315 SUPPORT Model Organism
"induces spreading of α-Syn pathology only through the autonomic pathway to both the central nervous system (CNS) and the autonomic innervation of peripheral organs bidirectionally"
Autonomic-to-central spread of seeded pathology.

name: Pure Autonomic Failure
creation_date: '2026-10-24T00:18:00Z'
description: >-
  Pure autonomic failure (PAF; Bradbury-Eggleston syndrome, idiopathic orthostatic
  hypotension) is a rare, sporadic, slowly progressive adult-onset alpha-synucleinopathy
  in which misfolded alpha-synuclein accumulates predominantly in peripheral autonomic
  neurons. Degeneration and dysfunction of postganglionic sympathetic noradrenergic
  neurons cause a profound deficit in norepinephrine synthesis and release, so that
  baroreflex-mediated vasoconstriction fails on standing. The clinical picture is
  dominated by disabling neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, often with paradoxical
  supine hypertension, accompanied by bladder, bowel, sexual and sudomotor failure, but
  without motor or cognitive signs of central neurodegeneration. PAF is frequently a
  prodromal state: about a third of patients phenoconvert to Parkinson disease,
  dementia with Lewy bodies, or multiple system atrophy over several years of
  follow-up. Treatment is symptomatic and aimed at orthostatic symptoms; no
  disease-modifying therapy exists.

pathophysiology:
- name: Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons
  description: >-
    Dopamine that leaks from storage vesicles into the neuronal cytoplasm is deaminated
    by monoamine oxidase to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (DOPAL), an obligate
    intermediate of dopamine metabolism normally detoxified by aldehyde dehydrogenase.
    DOPAL binds covalently to the lysine-rich alpha-synuclein molecule and oligomerizes
    it far more efficiently than dopamine itself does, and the resulting oligomers
    impair vesicular storage, returning more dopamine to the cytoplasm. This is the
    catecholaldehyde hypothesis, and it is the step put forward to explain why
    alpha-synuclein precipitates in catecholaminergic neurons rather than elsewhere.
    It is placed upstream of aggregation on in vitro, postmortem and computational
    grounds only: DOPAL has not been measured in sympathetic neurons of living
    patients, and whether it accumulates in PAF specifically is unresolved.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  mechanism_confidence: HYPOTHETICAL
  cell_types:

    term:

      label: sympathetic noradrenergic neuron

- name: Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation
  description: >-
    Misfolded, phosphorylated alpha-synuclein accumulates as Lewy bodies and Lewy
    neurites predominantly in peripheral autonomic neurons: sympathetic ganglion
    neurons and their distal axons in the heart, adrenal region, bladder and skin. CSF
    seeding assays are positive in nearly all patients, and cutaneous phosphorylated
    alpha-synuclein is found at every biopsy site. The initiating trigger is unknown.
    A rare clinically diagnosed case without any synuclein pathology shows that the
    clinical label is not always a synucleinopathy.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR

- name: Preganglionic Lesion Without Postganglionic Lewy Pathology
  description: >-
    In the minority of patients whose PAF is the premotor phase of MSA, the
    preganglionic autonomic lesion is not accompanied by postganglionic noradrenergic
    Lewy pathology. In MSA, insoluble alpha-synuclein is deposited in glia rather than
    as neuronal Lewy bodies. These patients have higher supine norepinephrine, a
    preganglionic pattern of sweat loss, severe bladder dysfunction and raised CSF
    neurofilament light chain, and they go on to MSA.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  notes: >-
    No cell type is bound: the glial alpha-synuclein pathology of MSA is documented in
    established MSA, not in patients who still carry the PAF diagnosis.

- name: Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect
  description: >-
    Surviving sympathetic terminals store and synthesize norepinephrine poorly. Forearm
    vein biopsies show normal norepinephrine transporter but very low tyrosine
    hydroxylase and reduced VMAT2, with a raised plasma DHPG:NE ratio; PET shows rapid
    loss of 18F-dopamine from residual cardiac nerves. Sympathetic dysfunction may
    therefore precede frank denervation.

  - target: Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity in Noradrenergic Neurons
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Failing vesicular sequestration returns dopamine to the cytoplasm, where monoamine
      oxidase converts it to DOPAL, so the storage defect feeds the autotoxic step that
      is proposed to have caused it. This closes a self-reinforcing loop rather than
      adding a one-way step, and the loop is the form in which the catecholaldehyde
      hypothesis is stated. The vesicular defect is measured in PAF patients; its
      consequence for DOPAL levels in those patients is not.
    hypothesis_groups:

    evidence:

      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      snippet: "DOPAL-induced AS oligomers impede vesicular functions (Plotegher et al., 2017), which could set the stage for a damaging positive feedback loop, destroying the neurons and resulting in a variety of clinical manifestations including parkinsonism and sympathetic neurocirculatory failure."
      explanation: >-
        States the feedback loop, and names sympathetic neurocirculatory failure, the
        clinical syndrome of PAF, as one of its outcomes.
    - reference: PMID:32372682

- name: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
  description: >-
    On standing, the baroreflex cannot increase sympathetic vasoconstrictor outflow or
    heart rate, so peripheral resistance and venous return fall and blood pressure
    drops. The heart-rate rise is blunted relative to the fall in blood pressure, which
    is the physiological signature that separates neurogenic from non-neurogenic
    orthostatic hypotension.
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: baroreflex arterial vasoconstriction on standing
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0001987
      label: vasoconstriction of artery involved in baroreceptor response to lowering of systemic arterial blood pressure
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29405350
    reference_title: "Orthostatic heart rate changes in patients with autonomic failure caused by neurodegenerative synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients with neurogenic OH had twice the fall in systolic blood pressure (SBP; -44 ± 25 vs -21 ± 14 mmHg ... p < 0.0001) but only one-third of the increase in HR of those with nonneurogenic OH (8 ± 8 vs 25 ± 11 beats per minute ... p < 0.0001)."
    explanation: Quantifies the blunted reflex response in synucleinopathy-related nOH, including PAF.
  - reference: PMID:39608812
    reference_title: "Cutaneous phosphorylated-synuclein: an early diagnostic biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Autonomic p-syn subscores correlated with orthostatic intolerance ratio on tilt (ρ=0.63, p=0.0004), blood pressure recovery time following Valsalva manoeuvre (r=0.44, p=0.03) and patient-reported orthostatic intolerance (ρ=0.57, p=0.006)."
    explanation: Cutaneous synuclein burden correlates with failed reflex blood pressure control; correlational, not causal.
  downstream:

    causal_link_type: DIRECT

  description: >-
    Loss of cardiac sympathetic nerves reduces the chronotropic and inotropic reserve
    of the heart. Denervated hearts show an impaired inotropic response to tyramine,
    which depends on endogenous norepinephrine release, and exaggerated responses to
    the direct beta-agonist isoproterenol.
  biological_scale: TISSUE

  - preferred_term: heart
    term:

      label: heart

    snippet: "Among patients with NOH those with cardiac sympathetic denervation have an impaired inotropic response to tyramine and exaggerated responses to isoproterenol."
    explanation: Functional consequences of cardiac denervation in PAF and PD with nOH.

- name: Adrenoceptor Denervation Supersensitivity
  description: >-
    Chronic loss of sympathetic input, combined with loss of baroreflex buffering, makes
    patients unusually sensitive to small doses of pressor and beta-adrenergic agents.
    This shapes treatment: norepinephrine replacers work at low doses, while exaggerated
    pressor responses contribute to supine hypertension on therapy.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR

    supports: SUPPORT

    snippet: "Denervation hypersensitivity and impairment of baroreflex buffering makes these patients sensitive to small doses of pressor agents."
    explanation: Review describing the clinical pharmacology consequence of denervation.

    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    snippet: "CV(R-R) was low in the MSA and PAF patients, but a significant difference was found only between the PAF and control groups."
    explanation: Reduced R-R interval variation in PAF.
  - reference: PMID:28202694
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure: Predictors of conversion to clinical CNS involvement."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Several variables were identified to predict conversion to MSA: (1) mild degree of cardiovagal impairment"
    explanation: A milder cardiovagal deficit points toward later MSA.
  downstream:
  - target: Decreased Heart Rate Variability
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
- name: Subclinical Central Catecholaminergic Involvement
  description: >-
    Even without motor signs, Lewy pathology and catecholaminergic loss are found in the
    substantia nigra and locus coeruleus. Nigral dopaminergic denervation is as severe
    as in Parkinson disease, but striatal terminals are relatively spared, which may
    explain the absence of parkinsonism. Hyposmia and REM sleep behaviour disorder are
    the clinical markers of this central involvement.
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: dopaminergic neuron
    term:
      id: CL:0000700
      label: dopaminergic neuron
  - preferred_term: noradrenergic neuron
    term:
      id: CL:0008025
      label: noradrenergic neuron
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:18363034
    reference_title: "Central dopamine deficiency in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Surprisingly, PAF and PD entail similarly severe nigral and overall central dopaminergic denervation. There is more severe loss of striatal dopaminergic terminals in PD than in PAF and more severe loss of sympathetic noradrenergic terminals in PAF than in PD."
    explanation: PET and postmortem evidence of nigral involvement with striatal sparing in PAF.
  - reference: PMID:39825743
    reference_title: "Central Involvement in Pure Autonomic Failure: Insights from Neuromelanin-Sensitive Magnetic Resonance Imaging and (18)F-Fluorodopa-Positron Emission Tomography."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "High-LR PAF patients showed reduced contrast in the LC and SN compared with controls and low-LR PAF patients, with values similar to PD and DLB."
    explanation: Neuromelanin MRI shows locus coeruleus and nigral loss in PAF patients at high risk of conversion.
  - reference: PMID:27757562
    reference_title: "A case series of REM sleep behavior disorder in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the presence of RBD suggests brainstem involvement in some cases of PAF"
    explanation: RBD indicates brainstem involvement.
  downstream:
  - target: Hyposmia
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
  - target: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
  - target: Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion)
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    hypothesis_groups:
    - lewy_body_paf
- name: Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion)
  description: >-
    In a subset of patients the synucleinopathy becomes clinically manifest in the CNS,
    and the diagnosis changes to Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or
    multiple system atrophy. Lewy-body PAF with cardiac noradrenergic denervation
    converts to Lewy body disease, whereas PAF with preserved postganglionic
    innervation, higher norepinephrine and an MSA-like CSF seeding profile converts to
    MSA. RBD is the strongest clinical predictor of any conversion.
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28093795
    reference_title: "Natural history of pure autonomic failure: A United States prospective cohort."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The presence of probable rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder was strongly associated with the development of a manifest central nervous system (CNS) synucleinopathy (odds ratio = 7.1)."
    explanation: RBD predicts conversion to a manifest CNS synucleinopathy.
  - reference: PMID:37843677
    reference_title: "Cardiac (18)F-dopamine positron emission tomography predicts the type of phenoconversion of pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All 6 patients with low cardiac 18F-dopamine-derived radioactivity who phenoconverted during follow-up developed a central LBD, whereas none of 4 patients with consistently normal 18F-dopamine PET phenoconverted to a central LBD (p = 0.0048), 3 evolving to probable MSA"
    explanation: Cardiac denervation status predicts the type of conversion.
  - reference: PMID:33881777
    reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Both NfL and the magnitude and reaction kinetics of αSyn PMCA faithfully predict which PAF patients will eventually phenoconvert to MSA."
    explanation: CSF markers predict conversion to MSA.
  - reference: PMID:42081229
    reference_title: "Phenoconversion in Pure Autonomic Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Hyposmia was the only predictor with diagnostic value to distinguish between those with phenoconversion to PD and DLB (hyposmia pooled risk ratio, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.26-2.97) and MSA, although rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and subtle motor signs were consistent predictors of phenoconversion to any central α-synucleinopathy."
    explanation: Pooled predictors of conversion and of its direction.
mechanistic_hypotheses:
- hypothesis_group_id: lewy_body_paf
  hypothesis_label: Lewy-Body PAF with Postganglionic Noradrenergic Lesion
  status: CANONICAL
  description: >-
    Most PAF is a peripheral Lewy body disease: intraneuronal alpha-synuclein
    aggregates in postganglionic sympathetic neurons cause noradrenergic denervation and
    very low norepinephrine. This form can phenoconvert to Parkinson disease or dementia
    with Lewy bodies, but not to MSA.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34669076
    reference_title: "Different phenoconversion pathways in pure autonomic failure with versus without Lewy bodies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Clinical and postmortem data show that the form of PAF that involves sympathetic intraneuronal synucleinopathy and noradrenergic deficiency can phenoconvert to PD or DLB-but not to MSA."
    explanation: Review of autopsy and clinical data defining the Lewy-body form.
- hypothesis_group_id: prodromal_msa_paf
  hypothesis_label: Non-Lewy PAF as Premotor Multiple System Atrophy
  status: ALTERNATIVE
  description: >-
    A minority of patients diagnosed with PAF have a preganglionic lesion without the
    postganglionic noradrenergic lesion: higher supine norepinephrine, normal cardiac
    sympathetic imaging, preserved smell, younger onset, severe bladder failure, raised
    CSF neurofilament light chain and an MSA-like seeding profile. These patients are in
    the premotor phase of MSA rather than having a peripheral Lewy body disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34669076
    reference_title: "Different phenoconversion pathways in pure autonomic failure with versus without Lewy bodies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Conversely, PAF without these features leaves open the possibility of premotor MSA."
    explanation: Defines the non-Lewy form as possible premotor MSA.
  - reference: PMID:28202694
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure: Predictors of conversion to clinical CNS involvement."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Several variables were identified to predict conversion to MSA: (1) mild degree of cardiovagal impairment, (2) preganglionic pattern of sweat loss, (3) severe bladder dysfunction, (4) supine norepinephrine >100 pg/mL, and (5) subtle motor signs at first presentation."
    explanation: Clinical and biochemical profile of PAF patients who convert to MSA.
  - reference: PMID:33881777
    reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "NfL at baseline was elevated only in patients who later developed MSA, perfectly separating those from future PD and DLB converters as well as non-converters."
    explanation: CSF NfL distinguishes future MSA converters.
  - reference: PMID:35790426
    reference_title: "Diagnosing Premotor Multiple System Atrophy: Natural History and Autonomic Testing in an Autopsy-Confirmed Cohort."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A third (5/15) were initially diagnosed with pure autonomic failure (PAF) before evolving into MSA. All these patients had normal supine plasma noradrenaline levels (332.0 ± 120.3 pg/mL) with no rise on head-up tilt (0.1 ± 0.3 pg/mL)."
    explanation: >-
      Autopsy-confirmed MSA cases first diagnosed as PAF had normal supine
      noradrenaline, the preserved-postganglionic profile that defines this hypothesis.
- hypothesis_group_id: catecholaldehyde_autotoxicity
  hypothesis_label: Catecholaldehyde (DOPAL) Autotoxicity as the Trigger for Aggregation
  status: EMERGING
  description: >-
    Aggregation in PAF is not the first event. On this account the initiating step is a
    shift of dopamine from vesicular stores into the cytoplasm, where monoamine oxidase
    produces the autotoxic aldehyde DOPAL; DOPAL then oligomerizes alpha-synuclein, and
    the oligomers further degrade vesicular storage, forming a positive feedback loop
    that destroys the neuron over a long preclinical period. The hypothesis is
    attractive for PAF because it explains the cell-type selectivity of the lesion, and
    because the vesicular storage defect it requires is independently measured in PAF
    patients. What is missing is any measurement of DOPAL in PAF neurons, and testing in
    animals has been obstructed by the secondary effects of the drugs used to
    manipulate the pathway. It is recorded as EMERGING for that reason, and the edges
    belonging to it are tagged so they can be read separately from the canonical chain.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34206133
    reference_title: "The Catecholaldehyde Hypothesis for the Pathogenesis of Catecholaminergic Neurodegeneration: What We Know and What We Do Not Know."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "DOPAL potently oligomerizes αS, and αS oligomers impede vesicular and mitochondrial functions, shifting the fate of cytoplasmic dopamine toward the MAO-catalyzed formation of DOPAL-destabilizing vicious cycles."
    explanation: Statement of the hypothesis, including the feedback loop that defines it.
  - reference: PMID:34206133
    reference_title: "The Catecholaldehyde Hypothesis for the Pathogenesis of Catecholaminergic Neurodegeneration: What We Know and What We Do Not Know."
    supports: NO_EVIDENCE
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "there has been insufficient testing of the catecholaldehyde hypothesis in animal models"
    explanation: >-
      The author of the hypothesis records that the animal work needed to test it has
      not been done, which is why this group is EMERGING rather than ALTERNATIVE. Graded
      NO_EVIDENCE because the sentence reports no animal result in either direction: it
      says the experiment is missing, not that it was run and the hypothesis failed.
  - reference: PMID:35621196
    reference_title: "Modeling the Progression of Cardiac Catecholamine Deficiency in Lewy Body Diseases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: COMPUTATIONAL
    snippet: "The model combines cardiac sympathetic activation with autotoxicity mediated by the dopamine metabolite 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde."
    explanation: >-
      A computational model of cardiac noradrenergic decline built on this mechanism
      reproduces serial 18F-dopamine PET data from Lewy body disease patients, PAF
      among them. Agreement of a model with data is indirect support for its mechanism.
- hypothesis_group_id: sympathetic_body_first_origin
  hypothesis_label: Sympathetic-Predominant Body-First Origin of the Pathology
  status: EMERGING
  description: >-
    Where the pathology starts, as distinct from what makes it start. Postmortem
    staging of Lewy body disease separates cases whose pathology appears first in
    peripheral autonomic tissue (body-first) from those where it appears first in the
    olfactory bulb and amygdala (brain-first), and splits the body-first group again
    into a vagal-predominant and a sympathetic-predominant subtype in roughly equal
    numbers. A purely peripheral, sympathetically dominated synucleinopathy, which is
    what PAF is, fits the sympathetic-predominant subtype, and this would make PAF the
    clinically isolated form of a distribution pattern that is otherwise observed on
    its way to Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. The evidence is
    autopsy-based and drawn from cohorts classified as incidental Lewy body disease,
    PD or DLB; no PAF case series has been staged this way, so the alignment is
    inferred rather than shown.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40082617
    reference_title: Sympathetic and parasympathetic subtypes of body-first Lewy body disease observed in postmortem tissue from prediagnostic individuals.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: "we identified two distinct body-first subtypes, one with vagal predominance and another with sympathetic predominance, in equal proportions"
    explanation: >-
      Establishes a sympathetic-predominant peripheral-onset subtype in 302 autopsied
      Lewy-positive cases. None was a PAF case, which is why this is indirect.
  - reference: PMID:40082617
    reference_title: Sympathetic and parasympathetic subtypes of body-first Lewy body disease observed in postmortem tissue from prediagnostic individuals.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: "In body-first LBD, isolated Lewy pathology in the sympathetic PNS is frequent, suggesting that the gut-to-sympathetic propagation route is as important as the vagal gut-to-DMV propagation route."
    explanation: >-
      Isolated sympathetic pathology with no central involvement is the anatomical
      counterpart of the PAF phenotype, and it is common rather than exceptional.
phenotypes:
- name: Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension
  category: Cardiovascular
  frequency: OBLIGATE
  diagnostic: true
  description: >-
    A sustained fall in blood pressure on standing or head-up tilt with a blunted
    heart-rate response, typically severe enough to cause syncope. It is the defining
    feature of the disease.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension
    term:
      id: HP:0004926
      label: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction
    clinical_course: PROGRESSIVE
  evidence:
  - reference: ORPHA:441
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "HP:0001278 | Orthostatic hypotension | Very frequent (99-80%)"
    explanation: Orphanet annotates orthostatic hypotension as very frequent.
  - reference: PMID:34669076
    reference_title: "Different phenoconversion pathways in pure autonomic failure with versus without Lewy bodies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "PAF is defined clinically by nOH without an identified secondary cause or clinical evidence of motor or cognitive impairment attributable to central nervous system neurodegeneration"
    explanation: nOH is the defining clinical criterion.
- name: Supine Hypertension
  category: Cardiovascular
  frequency: FREQUENT
  description: >-
    Systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or more (or diastolic 90 mmHg or more) when
    supine, falling on standing. It occurs in about half of patients without treatment
    and is worsened by pressor drugs; untreated it may cause hypertensive organ damage.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Neurogenic supine hypertension
    term:
      id: HP:0000822
      label: Hypertension
  notes: >-
    HPO has no supine hypertension term (runoak -i sqlite:obo:hp info "l~supine" returns
    nothing), so the parent Hypertension is bound and the posture is carried in
    preferred_term.
  sequelae:
  - target: Supine Pressure Natriuresis
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11927799
    reference_title: "Diagnosis and treatment of supine hypertension in autonomic failure patients with orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "about one half of these patients also suffer from supine hypertension"
    explanation: Frequency of supine hypertension in autonomic failure with orthostatic hypotension.
  - reference: PMID:15633433
    reference_title: "[Orthostatic hypotension and supine hypertension in pure autonomic failure]."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "On examination, orthostatic hypotension and supine hypertension were detected in the absence of pharmacological therapy. All the patients presented hypertensive organ disease."
    explanation: Case series of untreated PAF patients with supine hypertension and organ damage.
  - reference: PMID:29766366
    reference_title: "Consensus statement on the definition of neurogenic supine hypertension in cardiovascular autonomic failure by the American Autonomic Society (AAS) and the European Federation of Autonomic Societies (EFAS) : Endorsed by the European Academy of Neurology (EAN) and the European Society of Hypertension (ESH)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "In patients with neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, nSH is defined as systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg and/or diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg, measured after at least 5 min of rest in the supine position."
    explanation: Consensus definition of neurogenic supine hypertension.

    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: Defines the blunted heart-rate response of neurogenic OH.
