    snippet: "Patients with PAF had more severe orthostatic hypotension, lower supine plasma noradrenaline, and frequent sympathetic pupillary deficits at initial assessment than MSA and LBD."
    explanation: Pupillometry shows frequent sympathetic deficits in PAF.
- name: Anhidrosis
  category: Dermatological
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Anhidrosis
    term:
      id: HP:0000970
      label: Anhidrosis
  evidence:
  - reference: ORPHA:441
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "HP:0000970 | Anhidrosis | Very frequent (99-80%)"
    explanation: Orphanet annotates anhidrosis as very frequent.
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "median percentage anhidrosis of 51% (IQR 3-93%; N = 105)"
    explanation: Thermoregulatory sweat testing quantifies the extent of anhidrosis.
- name: Thermoregulatory Dysfunction
  category: Constitutional
  frequency: FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Thermoregulatory dysfunction
    term:
      id: HP:0004370
      label: Abnormality of temperature regulation
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "thermoregulatory dysfunction (N = 51; 38%)"
    explanation: Thermoregulatory symptoms in 38% of patients who remained PAF.
- name: Urinary Dysfunction
  category: Genitourinary
  frequency: FREQUENT
  description: >-
    Bladder symptoms occur in most patients; severe dysfunction with incontinence or
    catheterization is present in over a third and is a predictor of conversion to MSA.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Neurogenic bladder dysfunction
    term:
      id: HP:0000011
      label: Neurogenic bladder
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "bladder symptoms (N = 78; 59%), which were severe in 50 patients (37.6%) with incontinence or requiring catheterization"
    explanation: Frequency and severity of bladder dysfunction in patients who remained PAF.
  - reference: ORPHA:441
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "HP:0000020 | Urinary incontinence | Frequent (79-30%)"
    explanation: Orphanet annotates urinary incontinence as frequent.
- name: Constipation
  category: Gastrointestinal
  frequency: FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Constipation
    term:
      id: HP:0002019
      label: Constipation
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Additional autonomic symptoms included constipation (N = 60; 45%)"
    explanation: Constipation in 45% of patients who remained PAF.
  - reference: ORPHA:441
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "HP:0002019 | Constipation | Frequent (79-30%)"
    explanation: Orphanet annotates constipation as frequent.
- name: Erectile Dysfunction
  category: Genitourinary
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Sexual and erectile dysfunction
    term:
      id: HP:0008652
      label: Autonomic erectile dysfunction
  notes: >-
    Frequency is omitted because sources disagree: Orphanet annotates impotence as
    occasional, while a Mayo series reports sexual dysfunction (not restricted to men or
    to erectile failure) in 40%.
  evidence:
  - reference: ORPHA:441
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "HP:0000802 | Impotence | Occasional (29-5%)"
    explanation: Orphanet annotates impotence as occasional.
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "sexual dysfunction (N = 53; 40%)"
    explanation: Sexual dysfunction in 40% of patients who remained PAF.
- name: Nocturia
  category: Genitourinary
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Nocturia from supine pressure natriuresis
    term:
      id: HP:0000017
      label: Nocturia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36601916
    reference_title: "Continuous Positive Airway Pressure for the Treatment of Supine Hypertension and Orthostatic Hypotension in Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "was associated with lower nighttime diuresis (609±84 versus placebo 1004±160 mL; P=0.004)"
    explanation: >-
      Nighttime diuresis of about a litre on placebo, reduced by lowering nocturnal blood
      pressure, documents pressure-driven nocturnal urine output in autonomic failure.
- name: Normocytic Anemia
  category: Hematological
  description: >-
    Anemia with inappropriately low erythropoietin. The 38% figure comes from a mixed
    primary autonomic failure cohort, so no PAF-specific frequency is recorded.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Normocytic anemia with low erythropoietin
    term:
      id: HP:0001897
      label: Normocytic anemia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:8017744
    reference_title: "The anemia of primary autonomic failure and its reversal with recombinant erythropoietin."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Anemia was present in 32 of 84 patients (38%; 95% Cl, 27% to 50%)."
    explanation: Anemia in 38% of patients with primary autonomic failure (a group including but not limited to PAF).
  - reference: PMID:8017744
    reference_title: "The anemia of primary autonomic failure and its reversal with recombinant erythropoietin."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "mean corpuscular volume, 89 fL"
    explanation: Normal MCV indicates a normocytic anemia.
- name: Hyposmia
  category: Neurological
  description: >-
    Reduced smell identification, milder than in Parkinson disease in one series and
    similar in another; it predicts conversion to Lewy body disease rather than MSA.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hyposmia
    term:
      id: HP:0004409
      label: Hyposmia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19433741
    reference_title: "Hyposmia in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Hyposmia may be a feature of pure autonomic failure (PAF), but to a lesser degree than that found in Parkinson disease."
    explanation: UPSIT study of 16 PAF patients.
  - reference: PMID:19201246
    reference_title: "Olfactory dysfunction in pure autonomic failure: Implications for the pathogenesis of Lewy body diseases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The PAF group had a low mean UPSIT score (22+/-3), similar to that in PD (20+/-2) and lower than in MSA (31+/-2, p=0.004)."
    explanation: UPSIT scores in PAF were similar to PD.
- name: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
  category: Neurological
  frequency: FREQUENT
  description: >-
    Dream enactment behaviour is endorsed by about half of patients, usually years after
    the onset of orthostatic hypotension, and strongly predicts phenoconversion. An
    early small series found none, so the frequency depends on case selection.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: REM sleep behavior disorder
    term:
      id: HP:5200291
      label: REM sleep behavior disorder
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40053259
    reference_title: "The phenotype of \"pure\" autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Assessment of dream enactment behavior was completed in 86 patients and endorsed in 45 patients (52%)."
    explanation: Dream enactment in 52% of assessed patients who remained PAF.
  - reference: PMID:27757562
    reference_title: "A case series of REM sleep behavior disorder in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Five out of 8 (63 %) met diagnostic criteria for RBD, confirmed on vPSG."
    explanation: Polysomnography-confirmed RBD in a small PAF series.
  - reference: PMID:9598693
    reference_title: "REM sleep behaviour disorder differentiates pure autonomic failure from multiple system atrophy with autonomic failure."
    supports: REFUTE
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "RBD remained absent in the remaining six patients with pure autonomic failure."
    explanation: An early prospective series found no RBD in six PAF patients.
histopathology:
- name: Lewy Bodies in Sympathetic Ganglia and Distal Autonomic Axons
  description: >-
    Typical and atypical Lewy bodies in sympathetic ganglia and in distal autonomic
    axons (epicardial, periadrenal, bladder wall), with Lewy bodies also in substantia
    nigra and locus coeruleus despite the absence of motor signs.
  diagnostic: true
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:9255396
    reference_title: "The distribution of Lewy bodies in pure autonomic failure: autopsy findings and review of the literature."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Systemic autopsy results should be reviewed carefully in patients with PAF, as Lewy bodies in this disease may be seen in distal axons at a great length from their primary cell bodies."
    explanation: Autopsy finding of distal axonal Lewy bodies in PAF.
- name: Neuronal Loss in Intermediolateral Columns and Sympathetic Ganglia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:9255396
    reference_title: "The distribution of Lewy bodies in pure autonomic failure: autopsy findings and review of the literature."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "histopathologically by cell loss in intermediolateral columns and sympathetic ganglia"
    explanation: Characteristic neuronal loss in PAF.
- name: Cutaneous Phosphorylated Alpha-Synuclein in Autonomic Nerve Fibres
  description: >-
    Phosphorylated alpha-synuclein deposits in dermal autonomic nerves (sweat glands,
    arrector pili, blood vessels) on punch skin biopsy, with a heavier burden than in
    MSA and absence in non-synuclein autonomic neuropathies.
  diagnostic: true
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39608812
    reference_title: "Cutaneous phosphorylated-synuclein: an early diagnostic biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "P-syn was present in 22/22 (100%) PAF biopsies, 19/26 (73%) MSA biopsies and 0/22 (0%) non-synucleinopathy biopsies."
    explanation: Skin biopsy positivity in PAF, MSA and non-synuclein autonomic failure.
  - reference: PMID:23390175
    reference_title: "Skin sympathetic fiber α-synuclein deposits: a potential biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "all patients with PAF showed α-synuclein deposits, which were absent in patients with acquired autonomic neuropathy"
    explanation: Distinguishes PAF from acquired autonomic neuropathy.
imaging_findings:
- name: Reduced Cardiac Sympathetic Innervation on 18F-Dopamine PET
  modality: PET
  diagnostic: true
  description: >-
    Low myocardial 18F-dopamine-derived radioactivity indicates cardiac noradrenergic
    denervation. Low uptake predicts conversion to Lewy body disease, while normal uptake
    points toward MSA.
  located_in:
    preferred_term: heart
    term:
      id: UBERON:0000948
      label: heart
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16269589
    reference_title: "Cardiac and extracardiac sympathetic denervation in Parkinson's disease with orthostatic hypotension and in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Both the PD+OH group and the PAF group had decreased 6-(18)F-fluorodopamine-derived radioactivity in the heart (P < 0.0001)"
    explanation: Cardiac PET shows reduced sympathetic innervation in PAF.
  - reference: PMID:37843677
    reference_title: "Cardiac (18)F-dopamine positron emission tomography predicts the type of phenoconversion of pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Cardiac 18F-dopamine PET can predict the type of phenoconversion of PAF."
    explanation: Prognostic value of cardiac PET.
- name: Reduced Cardiac MIBG Uptake
  modality: OTHER
  notes: 123I-MIBG myocardial scintigraphy (planar or SPECT).
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  located_in:
    preferred_term: heart
    term:
      id: UBERON:0000948
      label: heart
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41072204
    reference_title: "Cardiac MIBG scintigraphy in pure autonomic failure: A systematic review."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "MIBG scintigraphy showed abnormal cardiac uptake in most patients with clinical PAF. Conversely, preserved MIBG uptake may be associated with a high probability of phenoconversion, particularly to MSA."
    explanation: Systematic review of 39 cases.
- name: Abnormal Dopamine Transporter SPECT Before Phenoconversion
  modality: SPECT
  description: >-
    DaTSCAN is abnormal in a subset of patients years before motor signs, and most of
    them go on to a more widespread synucleinopathy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40397689
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure: a natural history study of the Queen Square cohort."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall, 39% of patients had abnormal DaTSCAN results up to 7 years before phenoconversion, with 84% of these patients progressing to more widespread synucleinopathy."
    explanation: Prodromal striatal dopaminergic deficit on DaTSCAN.
- name: Reduced Neuromelanin MRI Signal in Locus Coeruleus and Substantia Nigra
  modality: MRI
  description: Seen in PAF patients at high risk of conversion, with values similar to PD and DLB.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39825743
    reference_title: "Central Involvement in Pure Autonomic Failure: Insights from Neuromelanin-Sensitive Magnetic Resonance Imaging and (18)F-Fluorodopa-Positron Emission Tomography."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "High-LR PAF patients showed reduced contrast in the LC and SN compared with controls and low-LR PAF patients, with values similar to PD and DLB."
    explanation: Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI evidence of early central involvement.
biochemical:
- name: Supine plasma norepinephrine
  presence: Decreased
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: plasma norepinephrine
    term:
      id: CHEBI:33569
      label: noradrenaline
  loinc_term:
    id: LOINC:14852-8
    label: Norepinephrine [Moles/volume] in Plasma
  notes: >-
    Very low supine values are typical of PAF. Published conversion thresholds are
    stated in mass units: supine norepinephrine above 100 pg/mL (Mayo) and at or above
    200 pg/mL (London cohorts) predict phenoconversion, especially to MSA. They are
    recorded here as prose rather than interpretation bands because the bound LOINC code
    is the molar plasma norepinephrine code.
  readouts:
  - target: Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: POSITIVE
    interpretation: Plasma norepinephrine at rest reflects postganglionic noradrenergic integrity.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:34176285
      reference_title: "Predictors of the Pressor Response to the Norepinephrine Transporter Inhibitor, Atomoxetine, in Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      snippet: "Plasma norepinephrine (NE) levels while resting supine, a biomarker of the integrity of sympathetic post-ganglionic neurons, are frequently normal in MSA but low in PAF and PD."
      explanation: Supine plasma NE as a readout of postganglionic integrity.
  - target: Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion)
    relationship: PREDICTS
    direction: THRESHOLD_DEPENDENT
    interpretation: Higher supine norepinephrine predicts conversion, particularly to MSA.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40696849
      reference_title: "Multimodal Autonomic Biomarkers Predict Phenoconversion in Pure Autonomic Failure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "50/194 (26%) with PAF phenoconverted to MSA or LBD after a median of 13 years, with normal pupils, heart rate response to deep breathing ≥ 10 bpm, and supine plasma noradrenaline ≥ 200 pg/mL predicting future phenoconversion to MSA or LBD"
      explanation: Supine noradrenaline threshold predicting phenoconversion.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28093795
    reference_title: "Natural history of pure autonomic failure: A United States prospective cohort."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The small group of patients retaining the pure autonomic failure phenotype had very low plasma norepinephrine levels"
    explanation: Very low plasma norepinephrine characterizes stable PAF.
- name: Plasma DHPG to norepinephrine ratio
  presence: Increased
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol to norepinephrine ratio
  readouts:
  - target: Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: POSITIVE
    interpretation: A raised ratio indicates intraneuronal norepinephrine metabolism exceeding vesicular sequestration.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:29162745
      reference_title: "Does sympathetic dysfunction occur before denervation in pure autonomic failure?"
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The finding of elevated plasma ratio of DHPG:NE and reduced VMAT2 in PAF indicates a shift towards intraneuronal NE metabolism over sequestration in sympathetic nerves"
      explanation: Links the ratio to the vesicular storage defect.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29162745
    reference_title: "Does sympathetic dysfunction occur before denervation in pure autonomic failure?"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "These findings were associated with a significantly higher ratio of plasma 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol (DHPG):NE in PAF participants when compared with controls (P<0.05)."
    explanation: Raised DHPG:NE ratio in PAF.
- name: CSF alpha-synuclein seeding activity
  presence: Present
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification (PMCA)
  readouts:
  - target: Peripheral Autonomic Alpha-Synuclein Aggregation
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: PRESENT_ABSENT
    interpretation: A positive seeding assay indicates aggregated alpha-synuclein; an MSA-like kinetic profile predicts conversion to MSA.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33881777
      reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The PMCA reaction was markedly different in five samples with maximum fluorescence and reaction kinetics previously described in MSA patients; all of these patients later developed MSA."
      explanation: Seeding kinetics distinguish future MSA converters.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33881777
    reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ASyn-PMCA was positive in all but two cases (94%)."
    explanation: CSF seeding is positive in nearly all PAF patients.
- name: CSF neurofilament light chain
  presence: Increased only in future MSA converters
  loinc_term:
    id: LOINC:100996-8
    label: Neurofilament light chain [Mass/volume] in Cerebral spinal fluid
  readouts:
  - target: Spread to Central Nervous System (Phenoconversion)
    relationship: PREDICTS
    direction: POSITIVE
    interpretation: Elevated CSF NfL at baseline predicts conversion to MSA.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33881777
      reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "NfL at baseline was elevated only in patients who later developed MSA, perfectly separating those from future PD and DLB converters as well as non-converters."
      explanation: CSF NfL separates future MSA converters.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33881777
    reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "NfL at baseline was elevated only in patients who later developed MSA"
    explanation: CSF NfL is normal in stable PAF and raised in prodromal MSA.
- name: Serum erythropoietin
  presence: Inappropriately low for hemoglobin
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: serum erythropoietin
  readouts:
  - target: Sympathetic Deprivation with Blunted Erythropoietin Response
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: NEGATIVE
    interpretation: Low erythropoietin relative to anemia reflects loss of sympathetic drive to erythropoietin production.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:8017744
      reference_title: "The anemia of primary autonomic failure and its reversal with recombinant erythropoietin."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "In seven of nine patients with autonomic failure who had hemoglobin levels less than 120 g/L, serum erythropoietin levels decreased below the 95% confidence interval corresponding to patients with iron deficiency anemia."
      explanation: Low erythropoietin in anemic autonomic failure patients.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:8017744
    reference_title: "The anemia of primary autonomic failure and its reversal with recombinant erythropoietin."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "No relation was found between serum erythropoietin and blood hemoglobin levels."
    explanation: Erythropoietin does not rise appropriately with falling hemoglobin.
diagnosis:
- name: Head-up tilt or active stand blood pressure testing
  description: >-
    Orthostatic hypotension is a sustained fall of at least 20 mmHg systolic or 10 mmHg
    diastolic blood pressure within 3 minutes of standing or head-up tilt. A blunted
    heart-rate rise (change in heart rate divided by change in systolic pressure below
    0.5 bpm/mmHg) identifies a neurogenic cause. Supine blood pressure is measured at
    the same session to detect supine hypertension.
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: Systolic blood pressure
    term:
      id: LOINC:8480-6
      label: Systolic blood pressure
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28717053
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Tilt table (head-up) testing is probably the test most commonly used to establish the diagnosis. However, simple office testing is also useful, such as having the patient stand after lying supine with blood pressure monitoring."
    explanation: Tilt-table and active-stand testing establish the diagnosis.
  - reference: PMID:29405350
    reference_title: "Orthostatic heart rate changes in patients with autonomic failure caused by neurodegenerative synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A ΔHR/ΔSBP ratio of 0.492 bpm/mmHg had excellent sensitivity (91.3%) and specificity (88.4%) to distinguish between patients with neurogenic from nonneurogenic OH (area under the curve = 0.96, p < 0.0001)."
    explanation: Heart-rate-to-blood-pressure ratio cut-off for neurogenic OH.
- name: Autonomic reflex screen and thermoregulatory sweat testing
  description: >-
    Cardiovagal, adrenergic and sudomotor testing quantifies the extent of autonomic
    failure. A postganglionic sweat-loss pattern fits PAF, whereas a preganglionic
    pattern and mild cardiovagal impairment predict conversion to MSA.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28202694
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure: Predictors of conversion to clinical CNS involvement."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Several variables were identified to predict conversion to MSA: (1) mild degree of cardiovagal impairment, (2) preganglionic pattern of sweat loss"
    explanation: Autonomic testing patterns that predict MSA conversion.
  - reference: PMID:31307617
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "We focus on various neurophysiological tests that may be used to evaluate the function of the peripheral autonomic nervous system including quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing, thermoregulatory sweat testing, and others."
    explanation: Review of the autonomic test battery used in PAF.
- name: Supine and standing plasma catecholamines
  description: >-
    Very low supine plasma norepinephrine with little rise on standing supports a
    postganglionic lesion and distinguishes PAF from MSA.
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: Plasma norepinephrine
    term:
      id: LOINC:14852-8
      label: Norepinephrine [Moles/volume] in Plasma
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40696849
    reference_title: "Multimodal Autonomic Biomarkers Predict Phenoconversion in Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients with PAF had more severe orthostatic hypotension, lower supine plasma noradrenaline, and frequent sympathetic pupillary deficits at initial assessment than MSA and LBD."
    explanation: Supine plasma noradrenaline is lower in PAF than in MSA or Lewy body disease, which is what makes the measurement discriminating.
- name: Skin biopsy for phosphorylated alpha-synuclein
  description: >-
    Punch biopsy immunohistochemistry detects phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in
    cutaneous autonomic nerves in essentially all patients with PAF, separating it from
    acquired autonomic neuropathies; a high total score separates PAF from MSA.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: skin biopsy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C51692
      label: Skin Biopsy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38506839
    reference_title: "Skin Biopsy Detection of Phosphorylated α-Synuclein in Patients With Synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "98.2% (54 of 55) with MSA, 96.0% (48 of 50) with DLB, and 100% (22 of 22) with PAF; 3.3% (4 of 120) of controls had cutaneous phosphorylated α-synuclein detected."
    explanation: Thirty-site blinded Synuclein-One study positivity rates.
  - reference: PMID:39608812
    reference_title: "Cutaneous phosphorylated-synuclein: an early diagnostic biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Total p-syn score >3 distinguished PAF from MSA with 100% specificity and 82% sensitivity."
    explanation: Quantitative score separates PAF from MSA.
- name: Cardiac sympathetic neuroimaging
  description: >-
    Cardiac 18F-dopamine PET or 123I-MIBG scintigraphy shows sympathetic denervation in
    most patients; preserved uptake raises the possibility of prodromal MSA.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: positron emission tomography
    term:
      id: NCIT:C17007
      label: Positron Emission Tomography
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37843677
    reference_title: "Cardiac (18)F-dopamine positron emission tomography predicts the type of phenoconversion of pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Since cardiac 18F-dopamine-derived radioactivity usually is low in LBDs and usually is normal in MSA, we hypothesized that patients with PAF with low cardiac 18F-dopamine-derived radioactivity would be more likely to phenoconvert to a central LBD than to MSA."
    explanation: Rationale for cardiac PET in classifying PAF.
- name: CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification and neurofilament light chain
  description: >-
    CSF seeding assays confirm a synucleinopathy, and an MSA-like seeding profile or
    raised NfL identifies prodromal MSA.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: lumbar puncture
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15327
      label: Lumbar Puncture
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: CSF neurofilament light chain
    term:
      id: LOINC:100996-8
      label: Neurofilament light chain [Mass/volume] in Cerebral spinal fluid
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33881777
    reference_title: "Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This finding has important implications not only for prognostication, but also for future trials of disease modifying therapies, allowing for differentiation of MSA from Lewy body synucleinopathies before motor symptoms develop."
    explanation: CSF testing separates prodromal MSA from Lewy body forms.
- name: Polysomnography and olfactory testing for central risk markers
  description: >-
    Video-polysomnography confirms RBD and smell identification testing detects
    hyposmia; both stratify the risk and direction of phenoconversion. A stricter UPSIT
    threshold improves the specificity of the MDS prodromal MSA criteria in PAF.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: polysomnography
    term:
      id: NCIT:C114185
      label: Polysomnography
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42444112
    reference_title: "Prospective Validation of the Movement Disorder Society Prodromal Multiple System Atrophy Criteria in Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Applying a stricter olfactory threshold improved specificity (90%-97%) and PPV (53%-83%), with a modest reduction in sensitivity (to 83%)."
    explanation: Olfactory testing refines prodromal MSA criteria in PAF.
  - reference: PMID:27757562
    reference_title: "A case series of REM sleep behavior disorder in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Five out of 8 (63 %) met diagnostic criteria for RBD, confirmed on vPSG."
    explanation: Polysomnography confirms RBD in PAF.
differential_diagnoses:
- name: Multiple system atrophy
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: multiple system atrophy
    term:
      id: MONDO:0007803
      label: multiple system atrophy
  distinguishing_features:
  - Central (preganglionic) lesion with preserved postganglionic innervation
  - Normal or near-normal supine plasma norepinephrine
  - Normal cardiac sympathetic imaging and preserved smell
  - Parkinsonism or cerebellar ataxia appear later; premotor MSA can present exactly as PAF
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24095130
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Cardiac sympathetic innervation is generally intact in MSA but decreased or absent in Parkinson's disease with autonomic failure and PAF."
    explanation: Cardiac innervation differs between MSA and PAF.
  - reference: PMID:19201246
    reference_title: "Olfactory dysfunction in pure autonomic failure: Implications for the pathogenesis of Lewy body diseases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The PAF group had a low mean UPSIT score (22+/-3), similar to that in PD (20+/-2) and lower than in MSA (31+/-2, p=0.004)."
    explanation: Smell is better preserved in MSA than in PAF.
- name: Parkinson disease with autonomic failure
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: Parkinson disease
    term:
      id: MONDO:0005180
      label: Parkinson disease
  distinguishing_features:
  - Shares postganglionic noradrenergic denervation with PAF
  - Parkinsonism with marked striatal dopaminergic terminal loss
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:18363034
    reference_title: "Central dopamine deficiency in pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Parkinsonism appears to reflect striatal dopamine deficiency rather than loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons per se."
    explanation: Striatal deficiency distinguishes PD from PAF.
- name: Dementia with Lewy bodies
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: Lewy body dementia
    term:
      id: MONDO:0007488
      label: Lewy body dementia
  distinguishing_features:
  - Cognitive decline with fluctuations and hallucinations
  - PAF may be its autonomic prodrome
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28093795
    reference_title: "Natural history of pure autonomic failure: A United States prospective cohort."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients presenting with pure autonomic failure are at high risk of phenoconverting to a manifest CNS synucleinopathy."
    explanation: PAF can evolve into DLB, PD or MSA.
- name: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: diabetic autonomic neuropathy
    term:
      id: MONDO:0001299
      label: diabetic autonomic neuropathy
  distinguishing_features:
  - Secondary autonomic neuropathy with an identified cause (diabetes mellitus)
  - No cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein on skin biopsy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34392300
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure and the differential diagnosis of autonomic peripheral neuropathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Peripheral autonomic manifestations are similar to those seen in other autonomic neuropathies, particularly, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, amyloid polyneuropathy, and autoimmune autonomic neuropathies."
    explanation: Names diabetic autonomic neuropathy as a principal mimic.
  - reference: PMID:23390175
    reference_title: "Skin sympathetic fiber α-synuclein deposits: a potential biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "all patients with PAF showed α-synuclein deposits, which were absent in patients with acquired autonomic neuropathy"
    explanation: Skin synuclein separates PAF from acquired autonomic neuropathies.
- name: Autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy
    term:
      id: MONDO:0016499
      label: autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy
  distinguishing_features:
  - Acquired autonomic neuropathy that mimics the peripheral autonomic picture of PAF
  - No cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein on skin biopsy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34392300
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure and the differential diagnosis of autonomic peripheral neuropathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Peripheral autonomic manifestations are similar to those seen in other autonomic neuropathies, particularly, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, amyloid polyneuropathy, and autoimmune autonomic neuropathies."
    explanation: Lists the main peripheral autonomic neuropathy mimics.
  - reference: PMID:23390175
    reference_title: "Skin sympathetic fiber α-synuclein deposits: a potential biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "all patients with PAF showed α-synuclein deposits, which were absent in patients with acquired autonomic neuropathy"
    explanation: Skin synuclein separates PAF from acquired autonomic neuropathies.
  - reference: PMID:39608812
    reference_title: "Cutaneous phosphorylated-synuclein: an early diagnostic biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "P-syn was present in 22/22 (100%) PAF biopsies, 19/26 (73%) MSA biopsies and 0/22 (0%) non-synucleinopathy biopsies."
    explanation: Non-synucleinopathy autonomic failure was skin-synuclein negative.
- name: Amyloid autonomic polyneuropathy
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: familial amyloid neuropathy
    term:
      id: MONDO:0007100
      label: familial amyloid neuropathy
  distinguishing_features:
  - Autonomic neuropathy that mimics the peripheral autonomic picture of PAF
  - No cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein on skin biopsy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34392300
    reference_title: "Pure autonomic failure and the differential diagnosis of autonomic peripheral neuropathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Peripheral autonomic manifestations are similar to those seen in other autonomic neuropathies, particularly, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, amyloid polyneuropathy, and autoimmune autonomic neuropathies."
    explanation: Amyloid polyneuropathy is a key differential.
  - reference: PMID:23390175
    reference_title: "Skin sympathetic fiber α-synuclein deposits: a potential biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "all patients with PAF showed α-synuclein deposits, which were absent in patients with acquired autonomic neuropathy"
    explanation: Skin synuclein separates PAF from acquired autonomic neuropathies.
  - reference: PMID:39608812
    reference_title: "Cutaneous phosphorylated-synuclein: an early diagnostic biomarker for pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "P-syn was present in 22/22 (100%) PAF biopsies, 19/26 (73%) MSA biopsies and 0/22 (0%) non-synucleinopathy biopsies."
    explanation: Non-synucleinopathy autonomic failure was skin-synuclein negative.
treatments:
- name: Patient Education and Physical Countermeasures
  description: >-
    First-line management: recognizing and avoiding triggers (heat, large meals,
    straining, sudden standing, vasoactive drugs), physical counter-manoeuvres, and
    planning upright activity. The aim is to reduce symptoms rather than normalize blood
    pressure.
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: patient education and orthostatic countermeasures
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15184
      label: Behavioral Intervention
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Cerebral and Muscle Hypoperfusion on Standing
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33705537
    reference_title: "Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "The first step in the management of NOH is to educate patients on how to avoid high-risk situations and providers to identify medications that trigger or worsen NOH."
    explanation: Education is the first management step.
  - reference: PMID:21664375
    reference_title: "Pharmacotherapy of autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Non-pharmacologic strategies such as physical counter-maneuvers, dietary changes (i.e. high salt diet, rapid water drinking or compression garments) are the first line therapy."
    explanation: Non-pharmacological measures are first line.
- name: Salt and Fluid Loading with Rapid Water Drinking
  description: >-
    Increased salt and fluid intake expands volume, and rapid drinking of about 500 mL
    of water raises blood pressure within minutes through the osmopressor reflex, which
    is exaggerated when baroreflex buffering is lost. Useful before standing or meals.
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: dietary salt and water loading
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15447
      label: Dietary Intervention
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21048076
    reference_title: "The osmopressor response to water drinking."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "The osmopressor response can be exploited in the treatment of orthostatic and postprandial hypotension in patients with severe autonomic failure."
    explanation: Review of the water-drinking pressor response in autonomic failure.
- name: Compression Garments and Abdominal Binder
  description: >-
    Lower-body and abdominal compression reduces venous pooling, increasing stroke
    volume and standing blood pressure.
  therapeutic_modality: DEVICE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: abdominal compression
    term:
      id: NCIT:C157735
      label: Compression Therapy
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:15241645
    reference_title: "Use of lower abdominal compression to combat orthostatic hypotension in patients with autonomic dysfunction."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Elastic abdominal binding increased standing blood pressure with 15/6 mmHg (range -3/3 to 36/14, p < 0.05)."
    explanation: Abdominal binder raised standing blood pressure in neurogenic OH.
- name: Head-Up Tilt Sleeping
  description: >-
    Raising the head of the bed reduces nocturnal supine hypertension and pressure
    natriuresis and may improve morning orthostatic tolerance. A scoping review judged
    the evidence weak, from small studies at high risk of bias.
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37626994
    reference_title: "The Impact of Head-Up Tilt Sleeping on Orthostatic Tolerance: A Scoping Review."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Orthostatic tolerance was consistently enhanced in OH studies with higher angles (≥12°)"
    explanation: Scoping review reporting improved orthostatic tolerance with steeper head-up tilt.
- name: Midodrine
  description: >-
    Peripheral alpha-1 adrenoceptor agonist (prodrug of desglymidodrine) that acts
    directly on vascular receptors and so does not require surviving noradrenergic
    terminals. Taken during the day before upright activity; avoid the supine position
    for several hours after a dose. Adverse effects include supine hypertension,
    piloerection and urinary retention.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: midodrine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:6933
        label: midodrine
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:9091692
    reference_title: "Efficacy of midodrine vs placebo in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. A randomized, double-blind multicenter study. Midodrine Study Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the evaluable patients, midodrine resulted in improvements in standing systolic BP at all time points (P<.001 at visits 2, 3, 4, and 5)"
    explanation: Multicentre randomized trial in neurogenic OH; the abstract gives no breakdown by diagnosis.
  - reference: PMID:9091692
    reference_title: "Efficacy of midodrine vs placebo in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. A randomized, double-blind multicenter study. Midodrine Study Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The main adverse effects were those of pilomotor reactions, urinary retention, and supine hypertension."
    explanation: Main adverse effects of midodrine.
  - reference: PMID:32979782
    reference_title: "Pharmacologic treatment of orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "patients with low \"sympathetic reserve\", i.e., those with peripheral noradrenergic degeneration (pure autonomic failure, Parkinson's disease) and low plasma norepinephrine, tend to respond better to \"norepinephrine replacers\" (midodrine and droxidopa)"
    explanation: PAF patients respond best to norepinephrine replacers.
- name: Droxidopa
  description: >-
    Oral synthetic amino acid converted by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase to
    norepinephrine outside noradrenergic terminals, replacing the missing
    neurotransmitter. Used for symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in PD,
    MSA, PAF and other autonomic neuropathies. Supine blood pressure rises and must be
    monitored.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: droxidopa
      term:
        id: CHEBI:31524
        label: droxidopa
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24944260
    reference_title: "Droxidopa for neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In patients with symptomatic nOH, droxidopa improved symptoms and symptom impact on daily activities, with an associated increase in standing systolic BP, and was generally well tolerated."
    explanation: Phase 3 trial including PAF patients.
  - reference: PMID:24944260
    reference_title: "Droxidopa for neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "At endpoint, supine systolic BP >180 mm Hg was observed in 4.9% of droxidopa and 2.5% of placebo recipients."
    explanation: Supine hypertension risk on droxidopa.
  - reference: PMID:28494751
    reference_title: "Integrated analysis of droxidopa trials for neurogenic orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Droxidopa improved virtually all nOH symptom scores compared with placebo, significantly reducing OHQ composite score (-2.68 ± 2.20 vs -1.82 ± 2.34 units; P < 0.001)"
    explanation: >-
      Pooled analysis of the three randomized trials (n = 460) behind approval for
      primary autonomic failure. The same analysis bounds its own claim: the trials
      assessed 2 to 10 weeks of treatment, and the authors note that a longer trial was
      then underway to confirm efficacy beyond that period, so this result does not
      establish durable benefit.
  - reference: PMID:27538531
    reference_title: "Analysis of number needed to treat for droxidopa in patients with symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The NNT for droxidopa for improvement in OHSA Item 1 was <10. The NNH for adverse events (AEs) leading to discontinuation in the pooled studies was 81."
    explanation: Number needed to treat and to harm from the pooled trials, which included PAF.
  - reference: PMID:25350981
    reference_title: "Randomized withdrawal study of patients with symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension responsive to droxidopa."
    supports: REFUTE
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In summary, this randomized withdrawal droxidopa study failed to meet its primary efficacy end point."
    explanation: The randomized withdrawal trial missed its primary dizziness endpoint, although secondary and post hoc measures favoured droxidopa.
- name: Fludrocortisone
  description: >-
    Mineralocorticoid that expands plasma volume through renal sodium retention. It
    raises blood pressure in both supine and standing positions, so it can worsen supine
    hypertension and should be used with caution.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: fludrocortisone
      term:
        id: CHEBI:50885
        label: fludrocortisone
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21664375
    reference_title: "Pharmacotherapy of autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "these interventions should be aimed at increasing intravascular volume either by promoting water and salt retention (fludrocortisone) or by increasing red blood cell mass when anemia is present (recombinant erythropoietin)"
    explanation: Fludrocortisone as a volume expander.
  - reference: PMID:15633433
    reference_title: "[Orthostatic hypotension and supine hypertension in pure autonomic failure]."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Salt-retaining steroid fludrocortisone, also, used to treat orthostatic hypotension, increases blood pressure both in supine and in standing position."
    explanation: Fludrocortisone worsens supine as well as standing blood pressure.
  - reference: PMID:33705537
    reference_title: "Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Volume expanders (fludrocortisone and desmopressin) should be used with caution."
    explanation: Caution with volume expanders.
- name: Pyridostigmine
  description: >-
    Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that enhances ganglionic transmission and so amplifies
    residual sympathetic outflow mainly when upright, with little effect on supine blood
    pressure. It is more effective with preserved sympathetic reserve, and therefore
    less so in PAF than in MSA or mild disease.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: pyridostigmine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:8665
        label: Pyridostigmine
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Failure of Baroreflex-Mediated Vasoconstriction
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16476804
    reference_title: "Pyridostigmine treatment trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Pairwise comparison showed significant reduction by pyridostigmine alone (BP fall of 27.6 mm Hg vs 34.0 mm Hg with placebo; P = .04)"
    explanation: Crossover trial in neurogenic OH; the abstract gives no breakdown by diagnosis.
  - reference: PMID:16476804
    reference_title: "Pyridostigmine treatment trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "No significant differences were seen in the supine BP, either systolic (P = .36) or diastolic (P = .85)."
    explanation: No worsening of supine blood pressure.
  - reference: PMID:33705537
    reference_title: "Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Drugs that enhance residual sympathetic tone (pyridostigmine and atomoxetine) are more effective in patients with mild disease and in MSA patients with spared postganglionic fibers."
    explanation: Reduced expected efficacy in PAF with postganglionic loss.
- name: Atomoxetine
  description: >-
    Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor that raises synaptic norepinephrine from
    residual sympathetic terminals. Acute doses raised upright blood pressure more than
    midodrine, but a four-week randomized trial showed no symptomatic benefit over
    placebo. Enhancers of residual sympathetic tone are expected to work better with
    preserved postganglionic fibres, although supine plasma norepinephrine alone did not
    predict the pressor response.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: atomoxetine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:127342
        label: atomoxetine
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25185131
    reference_title: "Efficacy of atomoxetine versus midodrine for the treatment of orthostatic hypotension in autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In contrast, atomoxetine produced a greater pressor response in upright systolic blood pressure (means difference=7.5 mm Hg; 95% CI, 0.6 to 15; P=0.03) compared with midodrine."
    explanation: Acute pressor efficacy in severe autonomic failure.
  - reference: PMID:39294522
    reference_title: "Atomoxetine on neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial."
    supports: REFUTE
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We found no differences in the OHQ composite score between atomoxetine and placebo at 2 weeks (-0.3 ± 1.7 versus -0.4 ± 1.5; P = 0.806) and 4 weeks (-0.6 ± 2.4 versus -0.5 ± 1.6; P = 0.251)."
    explanation: Four-week randomized crossover trial showed no symptomatic benefit (41% of participants had PAF).
  - reference: PMID:34176285
    reference_title: "Predictors of the Pressor Response to the Norepinephrine Transporter Inhibitor, Atomoxetine, in Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Nevertheless, our results showed that plasma NE is not a good predictor of response."
    explanation: Supine norepinephrine did not predict the atomoxetine pressor response.
  - reference: PMID:33705537
    reference_title: "Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Drugs that enhance residual sympathetic tone (pyridostigmine and atomoxetine) are more effective in patients with mild disease and in MSA patients with spared postganglionic fibers."
    explanation: Expected lower efficacy where postganglionic fibres are lost, as in PAF.
- name: Ampreloxetine
  description: >-
    Investigational once-daily selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that raises
    synaptic norepinephrine from residual sympathetic terminals. A phase 2 trial in
    neurogenic orthostatic hypotension raised seated blood pressure with little effect
    on supine pressure. The phase 3 SEQUOIA and REDWOOD trials, which enrolled PAF as
    well as PD and MSA patients, missed their primary endpoints. A prespecified MSA
    subgroup analysis showed maintained symptom benefit on secondary endpoints after
    randomized withdrawal; the trials were powered only for the full population, and no
    PAF-specific result has been reported. Like atomoxetine, it is expected to help
    least in PAF, where those neurons are lost. It is not approved.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: ampreloxetine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:757112
        label: ampreloxetine
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Deficient Sympathetic Norepinephrine Release
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34657222
    reference_title: "Safety and efficacy of ampreloxetine in symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: a phase 2 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Seated blood pressure increased 15.7 mmHg 4 h after ampreloxetine and decreased 14.2 mmHg after placebo [least squares mean difference (95% CI) 29.9 mmHg (7.6-52.3); P = 0.0112]."
    explanation: One-day randomized placebo-controlled phase of a 34-patient phase 2 trial; the abstract gives no breakdown by diagnosis.
  - reference: PMID:42475649
    reference_title: "Mechanism-Based Therapy With Ampreloxetine for Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension in Multiple System Atrophy: A Randomized Withdrawal Trial."
    supports: REFUTE
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Both SEQUOIA and REDWOOD did not meet their primary endpoints."
    explanation: >-
      The phase 3 programme enrolled patients with PD, PAF or MSA and failed its
      primary endpoints in the full population.
  - reference: PMID:42475649
    reference_title: "Mechanism-Based Therapy With Ampreloxetine for Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension in Multiple System Atrophy: A Randomized Withdrawal Trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The trials enrolled participants aged 30 years or older with PD, PAF, or MSA and symptomatic nOH."
    explanation: Confirms PAF patients were part of the phase 3 trial population.
  - reference: PMID:42475649
    reference_title: "Mechanism-Based Therapy With Ampreloxetine for Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension in Multiple System Atrophy: A Randomized Withdrawal Trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the trials were only statistically powered based on the full population analysis (PD, MSA, and PAF) and not for individual diagnoses"
    explanation: >-
      The basis for saying no PAF-specific efficacy result exists. The programme reported
      only an MSA subgroup, and was not powered for any single diagnosis, so nothing here
      measures the drug in PAF either way.
- name: Recombinant Erythropoietin
  description: >-
    Corrects the normocytic anemia of autonomic failure at low doses, increasing red
    cell mass and orthostatic tolerance.
  therapeutic_modality: PROTEIN_REPLACEMENT
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: epoetin alfa
      term:
        id: NCIT:C2695
        label: Epoetin Alfa
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Sympathetic Deprivation with Blunted Erythropoietin Response
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:8017744
    reference_title: "The anemia of primary autonomic failure and its reversal with recombinant erythropoietin."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Therapy with recombinant erythropoietin improved mean hemoglobin levels (from 108 to 133 g/L) in all patients treated (n = 5) at relatively low doses (25 to 50 units/kg body weight, subcutaneously, three times a week)."
    explanation: Open-label erythropoietin corrected anemia in autonomic failure.
- name: Nocturnal Treatment of Supine Hypertension
  description: >-
    Avoiding the supine position during the day, head-up tilt at night, and a
    short-acting antihypertensive at bedtime (for example transdermal nitroglycerin, or
    the mineralocorticoid antagonist eplerenone) lower nocturnal blood pressure without
    worsening daytime orthostatic hypotension.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: nitroglycerin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:28787
        label: nitroglycerin
    - preferred_term: eplerenone
      term:
        id: CHEBI:31547
        label: eplerenone
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Supine Hypertension Mechanism
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11927799
    reference_title: "Diagnosis and treatment of supine hypertension in autonomic failure patients with orthostatic hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "During the day, avoiding the supine position is often all that is required. Short-acting vasodilators (e.g., transdermal nitroglycerin) can be used during the night."
    explanation: Management approach to supine hypertension.
  - reference: PMID:28050656
    reference_title: "The recommendations of a consensus panel for the screening, diagnosis, and treatment of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension and associated supine hypertension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "provides essential recommendations based upon best available evidence as well as expert opinion for the (1) screening, (2) diagnosis, (3) treatment of nOH, and (4) diagnosis and treatment of associated supine hypertension"
    explanation: American Autonomic Society and National Parkinson Foundation consensus recommendations, which explicitly include pure autonomic failure.
  - reference: PMID:26644241
    reference_title: "Mineralocorticoid Receptor Activation Contributes to the Supine Hypertension of Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Eplerenone maximally reduced supine systolic blood pressure by 32±6 mm Hg at 8 hours after administration (versus 8±10 mm Hg placebo, P=0.016), with no effect on nocturia"
    explanation: Eplerenone lowered supine blood pressure in a crossover study (7 of 10 PAF).
  - reference: PMID:33687577
    reference_title: "Management Strategies for Comorbid Supine Hypertension in Patients with Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "Because nOH and nSH are hemodynamically opposed, therapies to treat one condition may exacerbate the other."
    explanation: Why supine hypertension treatment is confined to the night and balanced against daytime orthostatic hypotension.
- name: Nocturnal Continuous Positive Airway Pressure
  description: >-
    Overnight CPAP lowers supine blood pressure through a Valsalva-like reduction in
    cardiac output, reducing nocturnal diuresis and improving morning orthostatic
    tolerance.
  therapeutic_modality: DEVICE
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Supine Pressure Natriuresis
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36601916
    reference_title: "Continuous Positive Airway Pressure for the Treatment of Supine Hypertension and Orthostatic Hypotension in Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "overnight CPAP lowered nighttime systolic blood pressure (maximal change -23±5 versus placebo -1±7 mmHg; P=0.023) and was associated with lower nighttime diuresis (609±84 versus placebo 1004±160 mL; P=0.004) and improved morning orthostatic tolerance"
    explanation: Two-night crossover study in autonomic failure.
- name: No Disease-Modifying Therapy
  description: >-
    No treatment slows or prevents progression or phenoconversion. Biomarker
    stratification (cardiac imaging, CSF seeding and NfL, olfaction, RBD) is being
    developed to select prodromal patients for future disease-modification trials.
  therapeutic_modality: OTHER
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27338613
    reference_title: "Pure Autonomic Failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: "There is currently no specific treatment to stop progression in PAF."
    explanation: No disease-modifying therapy exists.
  - reference: PMID:37843677
    reference_title: "Cardiac (18)F-dopamine positron emission tomography predicts the type of phenoconversion of pure autonomic failure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This capability could refine eligibility criteria for entry into disease-modification trials aimed at preventing evolution of PAF to symptomatic central LBDs."
    explanation: Prognostic biomarkers aim at future trials.
